key_insight: Side-chain engineering controls annealing-induced packing changes in NDI-T2 oligomers, with shorter ethylhexyl chains supporting improved vertical electron transport.
engineering_relevance: Tuning side-chain length and thermal processing offers a molecular design strategy for improving electron transport through multilayer organic optoelectronic devices.
method: Compare ethylhexyl- and octyldodecyl-substituted oligomer films before and after annealing.
Probe morphology, packing and optical response using AFM, GIWAXS and steady-state spectroscopy, supported by TDDFT.
Measure vertical conduction with C-AFM and extract mobility using a space-charge-limited current model.
evidence_signal: Annealing improved vertical electron mobility in both materials; ethylhexyl-based films reached a maximum of 1.2 × 10⁻⁴ cm² V⁻¹ s⁻¹ and showed a smaller photoluminescence shift than octyldodecyl-based films.
watch_item: Mobility estimates depend on SCLC model assumptions, and performance in complete multilayer devices is not established by the abstract.
paper_title: Side-Chain Engineering Controls Molecular Packing and Vertical Electron Transport in Discrete n-Type NDI-T2 Oligomers
